# JOURNAL — optimizer handover (append-only, whole run)

YOU (the optimizer) own this file. It is the running, accumulating handover across ALL iterations — accepted AND rejected — and it is NEVER reset. Each iteration you APPEND one new entry at the bottom (under the marker line); you do NOT edit or delete earlier entries. Read the whole journal before proposing, so you build on EVERY prior attempt (not just the last accepted one) and never re-test a refuted idea.

You CANNOT know your own gate result while you write — the harness scores you AFTER you stop and stamps a **RESULT** line (outcome + Δ + the tasks you measurably broke/fixed, plus the ones whose move was too small to resolve) right below your entry. So do NOT write 'what worked' as a guess. To learn what actually worked, READ the framework RESULT lines of prior entries (and LEDGER.md): an entry whose RESULT says `rejected` with `broke={...}` tells you which specific edits to drop or redesign — its diff.patch is in ./prior_iterations/<id>/.

Append your entry for THIS iteration below the marker, using this shape (INTENT only — the framework appends the RESULT):

    ## Iteration <your candidate id> — <one-line headline of what you tried>
    - Changes I made (1 line per edit; name the file/tool + cluster it targets):
    - Per change, the EXPECTED effect + why it's safe (which failing task it should fix;
      why no passing task changes behavior):
    - Building on prior RESULTS: which prior entries' broke/fixed I used, and what I
      did NOT re-try because a prior RESULT showed it regressed (cite ids):
    - Refuted hypotheses (a prior RESULT proved this is NOT the fix — never re-test):
    - High-value clusters still NOT cracked (and the guard/tool designs already tried):
    - Plateau signal (are the last few RESULTs flat/negative? if so, which LEVER to switch
      to — e.g. a NEW composite tool instead of another guard, or prompt instead of code):
    - Focus next iteration:

## Iteration cand_0001 — deterministic baggage/payment guards in tools.py + one rebook-cancel prompt rule
- Changes I made (1 line per edit; file/tool + cluster it targets):
  - tools.py: new `_num_free_baggages(user, cabin, num_passengers)` helper encoding the membership×cabin free-bag table.
  - tools.py `update_reservation_baggages`: recompute `nonfree_baggages = max(0, total − free)` before charging (cluster: task 12).
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: same free-bag recompute (cluster: baggage, generalizes 12).
  - tools.py `book_reservation`: auto-reallocate the last payment when caller amounts ≠ computed total, so a stale-price total still writes correctly (cluster: task 25); plus enriched payment/balance/mismatch error messages.
  - policy.md "Modify flight": added "Replace-by-rebooking (cancel-and-rebook)" rule + worked example requiring `cancel_reservation` on the original (cluster: task 23).
  - tools.py docstrings: literal nonfree/payment formulas + worked example (doc-only).
- Per change, EXPECTED effect + why safe:
  - Baggage recompute → task 12 stops charging for free bags (gold nonfree=0). Safe: on correct inputs it reproduces the same value; verified 8/17/22 unchanged (nonfree stays 0, 0 charge entries).
  - Payment reallocation → task 25 books with the correct payment split in one turn. Safe: fires ONLY when caller amounts don't sum to the true price; task 8's exact-total call skips the branch entirely (payment unchanged).
  - Rebook-cancel prompt rule → task 23 agent cancels the original after rebooking. Safe: additive knowledge; no passing task performs a cancel-and-rebook, so their traces don't change.
- Building on prior RESULTS: none — iteration 1, LEDGER/RUNMAP/rejected.jsonl all empty.
- Refuted hypotheses: none yet (no prior RESULTs).
- High-value clusters still NOT cracked: tasks 37 & 40 (confirm-then-STOP terminal-turn artifact). Only lever is loosening the global confirmation policy, which is unbounded and would risk 8/11/17/22 — deliberately not attempted. Task 23 is a complex 3-way split; the prompt rule is plausible but lower-confidence than the 12/25 code fixes (DB-match is all-or-nothing).
- Plateau signal: n/a (first iteration). If this is rejected on 23, switch that lever from prompt → a composite tool or leave 23 uncracked; 12 and 25 are code-verified and should stand independently.
- Focus next iteration: confirm 12/25 landed via RESULT; if 23 didn't move, drop the prompt rule rather than expand it (avoid prose creep that could perturb passing modify tasks).
